subject: Evaluation gates and commit schedule — proposed commercial plan for Zenora
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jae Park <jae.park@zenora.ai>, Amelia Torres <amelia.torres@zenora.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@zenora.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation gates and proposed schedule (draft MAP)

Hi Jae / Amelia —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together a short, milestone-driven evaluation plan so we can align on success criteria and timing. Attached is a draft mutual action plan (Redwood_MAP_Zenora_v2.xlsx) and a short SOW stub. High level: 

- Kickoff & data prep (week 1–2): integration access + sample dataset ingestion.
- Pilot evaluation (week 3–8): 2-week focused use, then a 4-week ramp to target throughput.
- Decision milestone (week 10): technical signoff + business metrics met (latency < 250ms p95, inference cost target, retention/latency metrics).
- Commit & onboarding (by week 12): target initial committed capacity and pricing tier, with staged ramp and renewal uplift terms.

Proposed commercial guardrails linked to milestones:
- Pilot credit: $30k to cover evaluation token usage and engineering support.
- Commitment tiers: 3-month starter commit, 6-month predictable commit, enterprise annual commit (discounts increase with longer commitments).
- Ramp-based discounts: additional 5–10% discounts unlocked as usage sustainably exceeds agreed thresholds at 30/60/90 days post-commit.

I left placeholders for numbers in the SOW — happy to lock these with your procurement team. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Friday to walk through the MAP and pricing triggers? If helpful I can loop in Laura (CSM) for onboarding details and Markus (sales lead) for commercial approval.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Zenora_v2.xlsx, SOW_Zenora_draft.pdf

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Jae Park <jae.park@zenora.ai>

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation gates and proposed schedule (draft MAP)

Aditya —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side before Friday's call:

1) Pricing bands: can you provide concrete numbers for the starter commit vs. 6-month vs. annual? We need to map these to our forecast.
2) Uplift at renewal: what mechanics do you typically use for renewals when usage has materially exceeded the original commit? We want predictability (e.g., max 15% price step-up) and incentives for growth.
3) Ramp discounts: how strict are the measurement windows (30/60/90 days)? If our usage spikes after 90 days, can that still be considered for discounting?
4) Security/evidence: we need a short list of SOC2 artifacts and our compliance owner will follow up.

I'd like Amelia and Samir to be present on the call; they will own procurement/security scope.

—Jae
Head of Platform Engineering
Zenora AI
jae.park@zenora.ai

Forwarding Jae's clarifying questions — see below. Key asks we should answer on Friday: concrete $ amounts for starter/6mo/annual, an explicit renewal uplift cap and mechanics, and flexibility on the ramp measurement windows.

Questions for Markus/Laura: what is the most defensible way to present renewal uplift that keeps Zenora comfortable but preserves our ability to reprice when usages materially exceed commit? Also, do we have standard language for "late ramp" (usage increases after measurement window) that we can offer?

Thanks — Adi

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evaluation gates and proposed schedule (draft MAP)

Adi / Markus —

Suggested approach (concise):

1) Concrete numbers (example):
   - Starter commit (3 months): $60k committed spend, list price + 10% (no long-term discount).
   - Growth commit (6 months): $150k committed spend, 12% contract discount.
   - Enterprise annual: $360k committed, 18% contract discount + priority support.

2) Ramp-discount mechanics (practical, defensible):
   - Measurement windows at 30/60/90 days post-commit. Discounts are applied retroactively to the period once thresholds are met and sustained for at least two consecutive measurement points.
   - Late ramp allowance: usages that spike after 90 days are eligible for a one-time catch-up evaluation; discounts can be applied prospectively (not retroactively) unless usage meets a defined "sustained" bar over a 60-day window.

3) Renewal uplift cap + expansion credits:
   - Renewal uplift cap: standard uplift of up to +12% year-over-year unless customer signs a new multi-month commit that replaces previous terms.
   - Expansion credits: offer $25k EOS (expansion-on-success) credit for new seat/features if expansion is signed within 90 days of first commit. This preserves incentives to expand while limiting retrospective discounts.

4) Security artifacts: provide SOC2 Type II summary, pen-test statement, and security onboarding checklist. Laura can lead the artifacts package.

If Markus agrees, I recommend we present the example numbers to Jae as "illustrative" but with binding anchors for the ramp-discount mechanics and renewal cap — this addresses their ask for predictability while giving us movement on price for larger commits.

I'll be on the call Friday and can walk through onboarding/measures.

—Laura
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Updated MAP + commercial anchors (proposal)

Jae / Amelia / Samir —

Thanks for the questions — I pulled Laura and Markus' recommendations into an updated commercial anchor for the MAP. The attached spreadsheet contains the milestone calendar and the SOW stub with the anchors below. These are proposed, not final; happy to adjust on the call.

Commercial anchors (illustrative, to be finalized in SOW):
- Pilot credit: $30k (applied against first invoice if a commit is signed within 60 days of pilot end).
- Commit tiers (examples):
  * Starter (3 months): $60k committed spend, no contract discount.
  * Growth (6 months): $150k committed spend, 12% contract discount.
  * Enterprise (12 months): $360k committed spend, 18% contract discount + priority support.
- Ramp discounts: retroactive adjustments if usage meets thresholds at 30/60/90 days; sustained requirement applies (two consecutive measurement points).
- Renewal uplift: capped at +12% YoY unless a new larger multi-month commit is executed; we will include a clause to re-open pricing if usage exceeds modeled forecast by >200% for >90 days.
- Expansion credits: $25k credit available for expansion signed within 90 days of initial commit.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached MAP and SOW draft.
- Call Friday 10:00am PT to finalize anchors and agree on procurement timeline.
- If these anchors look reasonable, I will generate a DocuSign-ready SOW with the numbers populated (link included).

Adi —

This looks good; the anchors help a lot. A couple of small asks before the call:

1) Can you add an explicit example that shows the math for a 6-month Growth commit (list price -> discount -> expected monthly spend) so procurement has something quantifiable?
2) The renewal uplift cap is acceptable but can we add language that caps uplift at +12% or the CPI index, whichever is lower? That helps our CFO model for inflation volatility.
3) On expansion credits: will those apply to additional model types (e.g., embeddings) or only additional capacity? We prefer credits that can be used across product lines.

If you can add those clarifications into the SOW (or a short one-page commercial summary) ahead of the call, we'll be able to move quickly. We're broadly aligned and aiming to close this evaluation-to-commit within the quarter.

Thanks —
Jae

On behalf of Zenora AI
